---
title: "Before the session"
---
The session is worked in R, inside an IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.), on a ready-made workspace that you download and check by following the setup page. The data ship inside the workspace, so there is nothing to register for and nothing else to download. The session sets aside only a few minutes for the setup check, so the installation has to work before you arrive. The browser lab runs the same exercise in a browser tab and gives the same numbers. The facilitator uses it on the shared screen, and it is the place to carry on if a machine fails.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| [Setup](../../setup.qmd) | Install R and an IDE, download the workspace zip and run `R/check_setup.R` until it prints OK. Open the [browser lab](../../cases/housing/lab.qmd) once as well and confirm that it loads on the machine you will use. The [help page](../../help.qmd) has the problems that other participants have met. | 30 to 60 minutes, once |
| [Case study](../../cases/housing/index.qmd) | The original study and its design, SCORE and the Multi100 project, the five reanalyses and the question that each of them answered, how their results were put on one scale, and the replication with new data. The session works on this case throughout and can give it only a few slides. | 45 minutes |
| [Exercise overview](../../cases/housing/exercise.qmd) | Read the claim that you will be working on and the table of what the five Multi100 analysts found when they reanalysed it. | 10 minutes |
| [Getting started with R](../../companion/intro-r.qmd) | Optional. Worth the time if you have never written R: objects, data frames, reading a CSV file, the pipe and a first table, all on the housing-audit data. | An evening |
| [Positron, RStudio and VS Code](../../companion/ide.qmd) | Optional. Where the console, the variables and the data viewer are in the IDE that you chose. | 30 minutes |

**By the start of the session** you have the workspace working on the machine that you will use, and you know what the claim is and how the five Multi100 analysts came to different conclusions about it.
